title: Haveningry Review 2026: Red Flags, Fees & Real Verdict
description: Haveningry review for Australians: 250 minimum deposit, fees, and what the site leaves out about its licence, support hours and operator.
author: Olivia Bennett
content:
Haveningry presents itself as the official AI-powered cryptocurrency trading platform for Australia. Its site promises automated trading, a low entry point and 24/7 access, and it names no regulator.

This review summarises what the Haveningry site says about its method, costs, payments and support, points out where its own pages disagree with each other, and lists the checks Australian readers should run before registering.

Haveningry Explained: What the Site Describes

According to its site, Haveningry is an AI-powered platform that scans markets, identifies opportunities and executes trades automatically based on the risk level you choose. A manual mode is also offered, and you can switch between the two.

The home page positions it as an official trading platform for Australia, with cryptocurrencies such as BTC, SOL and USDT named first and equities, forex, commodities, precious metals and CFDs listed as well.

Platform Overview

Category Description
Platform Type AI-powered trading platform, per the site
Minimum Deposit 250 (the site does not state the currency)
Registration Fee None, per the FAQ

Payment Methods Credit and debit cards, bank transfer, PayPal, e-wallets
Support 24/7 on the home page; Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 on the About page
Mobile Access No separate app mentioned; works in desktop and mobile browsers
Security Claims SSL 256-bit, TLS 1.3, two-factor authentication, 98% of assets in offline wallets
Address Shown 59-60 Grosvenor Street, Mayfair, London (About page)

Everything in this table is what the site states. We have not tested any of it and could not confirm it independently.

Haveningry: Where It Delivers, Where It Doesn’t

Fair reviews cut both ways. Here is what the site offers, and what does not add up.

Haveningry strengths, per its site:

  • No registration fee is stated in the FAQ.
  • Automated and manual trading modes are both offered.
  • Cards, bank transfer, PayPal and e-wallets are listed as ways to fund the account.
  • Two-factor authentication is mentioned for account security.
  • The risk page openly describes volatility, leverage and total-loss risk.

Where Haveningry Falls Short:

  • No regulator, licence number or registration number is named, although the home page says the platform is licensed in Australia.
  • Support hours differ between pages: 24/7 on the home page, weekdays only on the About page.
  • The site targets Australia but shows a London address and no company name.
  • Performance figures such as 85% accuracy and 14% to 19% returns come with no method or audit.
  • The risk page calls the site an information and marketing platform and refers to third-party advertisers.

A confident home page is not a credential. Judge Haveningry on the details it can back up, not on the figures it advertises.

What Actually Happens Behind Haveningry

The site says the platform runs continuously, analyses markets and places trades when conditions match your settings. You choose an asset, an amount, and optional stop-loss and target prices, or switch on automated trading at a chosen risk level.

The FAQ adds that continuous analysis reduces the need for monitoring, but that you should still review your account regularly. The risk page goes further and says bots can malfunction and that users are responsible for watching them.

None of this describes the method in a way that can be checked, so treat the automation as a claim, not a feature we have confirmed.

Getting Set Up: What the Process Looks Like

This is the sign-up flow as the Haveningry site describes it. We did not go through it ourselves.

1. Sign up

Enter your name, email and phone number, verify your email, set a password and switch on two-factor authentication.

2. Deposit funds

The minimum deposit is 250. The site says a first deposit may trigger an ID verification step.

3. Configure and trade

Choose an asset, set an amount with stop-loss and target prices, or enable automated trading based on your chosen risk level.

Registration needs a phone number, so expect a call or message after you sign up. Keep any first deposit small while you see how the account behaves.

Breaking Down What Haveningry Costs

The FAQ says there is no registration fee, and the home page says there are no subscription fees and no hidden charges. The same page also says minimal transaction or withdrawal fees apply where applicable, and the FAQ adds that other charges may apply.

No fee schedule is shown, only a promise that you will see the fees before you proceed. Before you deposit, look for:

  • The spread or commission on each trade.
  • Withdrawal fees and the minimum withdrawal amount.
  • Currency conversion charges if the deposit is not in your own currency.
  • Any inactivity or account maintenance fee.

The ROI calculator on the home page shows a profit of 250 on a 250 deposit after 50 days. Treat that as marketing, not as a projection.

Which Assets Haveningry Covers

The site names cryptocurrencies first, with BTC, SOL and USDT on the home page and Bitcoin and Ethereum in the FAQ. Its capabilities section also lists equities, forex, commodities, precious metals and CFDs, and mentions 65+ currencies.

We could not confirm which of these are actually available to you, or through which broker or exchange the trades are placed. Check the list inside your account before you rely on any of it:

  • Which assets and pairs you can really trade, and whether CFDs are offered to retail clients in your country.
  • Whether trades are placed through a named broker or exchange.
  • Whether spreads and charges differ by asset.

Is Haveningry Legit in Australia?

The home page says Haveningry is licensed and compliant with financial regulations in Australia and fully registered there. It does not name a regulator, a licence number or a registration number, and the site does not give a legal entity name.

Other pages do not line up with that picture:

  • The About page gives a London address, not an Australian one.
  • The risk page describes the site as an information and marketing platform and mentions third-party advertisers.
  • Support is shown as 24/7 on the home page and as weekdays only on the About page.
  • The FAQ says withdrawals depend on account verification and provider processing, while the home page says there are no restrictions on when or how often you can withdraw.
  • The home page claims 98+ supported countries while presenting itself as the official platform for Australia.

In Australia, businesses offering financial products to retail clients generally need an Australian Financial Services licence from ASIC. We could not confirm that Haveningry holds one. Checks you can run yourself:

  • Search the company name and any licence number on ASIC’s Financial Services Register.
  • Check ASIC’s investor alert list for the name and the website address.
  • Search the name on Scamwatch and MoneySmart for scam reports.
  • Check whether the firm belongs to the Australian Financial Complaints Authority (AFCA).
  • If you rely on the London address, look the company up on the UK Financial Conduct Authority’s register.
  • Look up when the domain was registered, since a very new domain deserves extra care.

Legitimacy and profitability are different things. Even a properly licensed platform can lose you money if you overcommit or rely on best-case figures. This section is general information, not legal or financial advice.

Mistakes Worth Avoiding on Haveningry

Most of the losses with automated trading tools trace back to user decisions, not the platform itself. A few worth flagging:

Assuming the name means the platform is established.

A memorable brand is not a substitute for checking the platform’s actual history and terms.

Funding well beyond the minimum right away.

Test the platform on your own terms before scaling up. That is exactly why a small first deposit makes sense.

Treating AI-assisted trading as fully hands-off.

Check your open positions regularly. Market conditions shift, and settings that worked last month may not fit now.

Ignoring fees and spreads.

Small per-trade costs add up once you make a reasonable number of trades. Read the current terms first.

Skipping a small test withdrawal.

Payout terms are easy to overlook until you need them. Try a small withdrawal while the amount is still low.

A Quick Checklist Before Your First Live Trade

Run through this before committing real funds.

  • Licence or registration number found and checked on the regulator’s own register.
  • Support hours and withdrawal terms confirmed in writing, since the site gives two versions.
  • Fees and spreads read in the current terms before the first deposit.
  • Account verified, with a strong, unique password and two-factor authentication on.
  • First deposit kept to the 250 minimum.
  • A small withdrawal tested early, before depositing more.
  • Performance claims treated as marketing until a method is shown.

Who Gets the Most Out of Haveningry

Haveningry may suit a newcomer who wants a low entry point of 250, will read the terms first and is prepared to verify the company independently before depositing.

It is a poor fit for anyone who needs a confirmed regulator and a named operator, who plans to rely on the advertised returns, or who wants an income they can leave on autopilot.

The platform underneath the claims is unconfirmed. Judge it on what you can check, not on the branding.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Haveningry legit?

We could not confirm it. The site says it is licensed and compliant in Australia but names no regulator or licence number, so check ASIC’s Financial Services Register before you deposit.

Is Haveningry a scam?

We cannot say either way. Several statements on the site conflict with each other and no operator can be confirmed, so start small, test a withdrawal early and register only through the official website.

Is Haveningry legit in Australia?

The site presents itself as the official platform for Australia, but it shows a London address and we could not confirm an AFS licence. Check ASIC’s register and investor alert list first.

What is the Haveningry minimum deposit?

250, according to the site. The site does not state the currency.

Does Haveningry charge fees?

The site says there is no registration fee and no hidden charges, but also that minimal transaction or withdrawal fees apply where applicable. No fee schedule is shown.

How do I withdraw from Haveningry?

The site says you can request a withdrawal through the same payment provider you used to deposit, subject to account verification and processing times. No timeframe is given.

Does Haveningry have a mobile app?

No separate app is mentioned. The site says the platform works across desktop and mobile devices in a browser.

What payment methods does Haveningry accept?

Credit and debit cards, bank transfer, PayPal and e-wallets are listed on the site.

How do I log in to Haveningry?

Use the sign-in page on the official Haveningry website with the email and password you set at registration, and turn on two-factor authentication. Check the address before you enter any details.

Does Haveningry guarantee profits?

No. The risk page itself says no return is guaranteed and that you can lose all of your investment. Treat the advertised returns and accuracy figures as marketing.

Where We Land on Haveningry

Haveningry offers a familiar AI-assisted pitch with a low 250 entry point and no registration fee, according to its own site. What it does not offer is a named regulator, a legal entity or consistent support and withdrawal details.

If you decide to try it, keep the first deposit small, confirm the licence on ASIC’s register, and test a withdrawal before you add funds.
